title: Verbs: the prefixes N- and di-
title_target: Kecap pagawéan: rarangkén N- jeung di-
goal: Make active and passive verbs from roots, and use the suffixes *-keun* and *-an* (cousins of Indonesian *-kan* and *-i*).
bekal: how the prefix N- changes shape with the first letter of the root
the suffixes *-keun*, *-an*, and *-eun* — the last has no English equivalent

dialogs.title: Paguneman — Helping Bu Imas
dialogs.intro: Sunday morning. Bu Imas is clearing out the storeroom and Rani offers to help. This short conversation contains nine verbs with prefixes or suffixes.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.id: Ma'am, is there anything I can help with?

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Eh, nuhun Néng. Ieu Ibu keur mérésan gudang.
lines.id: Oh, thanks, Néng. I'm tidying up the storeroom.
lines.literal: oh, thanks Néng. this Ma'am is tidying storeroom.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Mangga, sapuan waé heula. Ibu mah rék mindahkeun lomari.
lines.id: Go ahead, just sweep first. I'm going to move the wardrobe.
lines.literal: please, swept just first. Ma'am [mah] will move wardrobe.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Éta lomari beurat teuing, Bu. Hayu urang angkat duaan.
lines.id: That wardrobe is too heavy, ma'am. Let's lift it together.
lines.literal: that wardrobe heavy too, Ma'am. come-on we lift both.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Sok atuh. Cekel nu palih ditu, Ibu nu dieu.
lines.id: All right then. You hold that side, I'll take this one.
lines.literal: go-ahead atuh. hold which side there, Ma'am which here.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Hiji, dua, tilu… Aduh, beurat pisan!
lines.id: One, two, three… Oof, it's really heavy!
lines.literal: one, two, three… oof, heavy very!

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Ulah dipaksakeun. Simpen waé di dieu heula.
lines.id: Don't force it. Just put it down here for now.
lines.literal: don't forced. put just at here first.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.id: What should I do with these books, ma'am? Throw them out?

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Ulah dipiceun. Dibikeun waé ka madrasah. Aya nu maca deui.
lines.id: Don't throw them out. Just give them to the madrasa. Someone will read them again.
lines.literal: don't thrown-away. given just to madrasa. there-is who read again.

lines.speaker: Rani:
lines.text: Saé pisan. Abdi nu ngantunkeun ka ditu engké.
lines.id: That's great. I'll take them over there later.
lines.literal: good very. I who deliver to there later.

lines.speaker: Bu Imas:
lines.text: Nuhun pisan, Néng. Ku Ibu didoakeun sing lancar sagalana.
lines.id: Thank you so much, Néng. I pray everything goes smoothly for you.
lines.literal: thanks very, Néng. by Ma'am prayed-for may smooth everything.

notes: **Dibantosan** from *bantos* (help, lemes) + *di-…-an*. The loma form is *dibantuan*, from *bantu*. The suffix *-an* here doesn't make a noun; it marks an action done to or for a person.
**Mérésan** from *bérés* (tidy, done) → *N-* + *bérés* + *-an* = to tidy up. The *b* melts into *m*: *bérés* → *mérésan*. This "melting" pattern is explained in the grammar box.
**Dikumahakeun** from *kumaha* (how) — literally "be how-ed", i.e. "what should be done with it?". Even question words can take affixes, a very Sundanese feature with no parallel in English.
**Dipiceun** = thrown away, from *piceun*. The active form is *miceun*. ⚠️ Don't confuse it with *mikeun*/*dibikeun* (give/given), which sounds similar but means the opposite.

**Ngantunkeun** has two meanings, told apart by context: **to take someone/something somewhere** (from *antun*) and **to leave behind / pass away** (a gentle word for dying). In this dialogue it's the first.

**Ku** marks the doer in a passive sentence: *ku Ibu didoakeun* = "prayed for by me (Ma'am)". It's like English "by", and it can go at the front of the sentence — in fact that's the most common order.

grammars.title: The prefix N-: one prefix, five shapes
body: Grammar books write the Sundanese active-verb prefix as **N-**, but its shape changes with the first letter of the root — much as English "in-" becomes "im-" in *impossible* and "il-" in *illegal*, only more systematically.

head: First letter
Shape of N-
Root
Becomes
Meaning
rows: to tidy up, to steam in leaves
l, r, m, n, w, y

after: The good news: the pattern is **regular**, so once you know it your guesses will usually be right. (If you know Indonesian, it works much like *me-/mem-/men-/meng-/meny-*; the extra shape **nga-** is used for roots starting with *l, r, m, n, w, y*, and freely with many other words.)

⚠️ Some very common words have irregular forms to memorize: *dahar* → **ngadahar** (not *nahar*), *bawa* → **mawa**, *béré* → **méré**, *indit* → **indit** (no prefix), *balik* → **balik** (no prefix). Verbs of motion like *indit*, *balik*, *datang*, *diuk* don't take the prefix at all.

The passive is much easier: **di-** is simply attached with no changes. *tulis* → *ditulis* (written), *bawa* → *dibawa* (carried), *piceun* → *dipiceun* (thrown away). The doer is marked with **ku**: *ditulis ku kuring* = written by me.

head: Suffix
Function
Example
Meaning
rows: something to be / that must be

blocks.text: **-keun** often works like English "-ify" or "for someone" (and matches Indonesian *-kan*); **-an** suggests repetition or an action aimed at someone (like Indonesian *-i*). You'll usually guess them right from context. What's truly new is **-eun**.
**-eun** has no real equivalent, and it is very productive. Attach it to a verb to make "a thing to be…-ed":

The last three rows use the combination **pika-…-eun**, meaning "making people…" — much like English "-ing" in *heartbreaking*, *frightening*. It's very often used to judge things: *pikaresepeun* (pleasant), *pikabungaheun* (delightful), *pikangeunaheun* (comfortable).

blocks.title: Sentences with prefixed and suffixed verbs
items: **Abdi nuju nyerat serat.** — I'm writing a letter.
**Bukuna dibaca ku adi.** — The book is being read by my little brother/sister.
**Tulung candakkeun cai.** — Please fetch me some water.
**Aya daharaneun teu?** — Is there anything to eat?
**Pilemna pikaseurieun pisan.** — The film is really funny.

exercises.prompt: Make the active verb with the right form of N-.
Turn into a passive sentence with di- and ku.
Make a noun with the suffix -eun.
Put the words in the right order.
